evidence: app/package.json:11 — exact pin of @gracile/gracile 0.11.0, the current stable (npm latest, published ~6 months ago per npmjs.com on 2026-10-30); every route is written against this pre-1.0 surface
app/package.json:14 — vite ^8.3.5: Vite 8 major line stable only since Mar 2026, central to the entire build/SSR pipeline (app/vite.config.js:5)

app/vite.config.js:5 — only documented stable plugin options (output: 'server', trailingSlash: 'ignore', the latter the documented default); Gracile's sole experimental flag, experimental.generateRoutesTypings, is unused
app/src/routes/(home).client.js:30,40-50,68-71 — interactivity hand-rolled with long-stable fetch/DOMParser/history instead of the CSR add-on that Gracile docs mark 'under an experimental phase'

app/src/document.js:14 — the single reach outside the documented stable surface: Vite's new URL(url, import.meta.url) asset pattern, which Vite docs state 'does not work with SSR' (confirmed broken in app/dist/server/chunk/document.js:12)
reach.rationale: The code reaches for zero experimental/preview APIs — notable restraint on a framework that offers several — but everything sits on recently-stable software: a pre-1.0 framework whose stable release is ~6 months old and a Vite major line ~7.5 months old, both in the most central places.

evidence: app/src/document.js:1-6 — one shared document module wired into all seven routes, so framework changes to the document/template contract are fixed in one place
app/src/lib/api.js:3 — all API access (including the in-memory cache) isolated behind one plain-module data layer with no framework coupling
app/src/lib/components.js:1-38 — all shared Lit templates in one module, using only long-stable core html and ?attr bindings (app/src/routes/(home).js:148)
app/server.js:8,15 — the whole Node/Express adapter surface confined to one file, matching the documented adapter verbatim
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].client.js:1-14 — client scripts are framework-free vanilla DOM and survive any framework churn unchanged

app/src/routes/(home).js:15 — deduction: the BUILDING()/GRACILE_BUILD guard is copy-pasted into six route handlers (also [name].js:23, types/index.js:7, types/[name].js:13, moves/[name].js:18, abilities/[name].js:15) instead of one shared helper
containment.rationale: Framework-coupled code is channeled through a single document, data and components module plus one 6-line config and one adapter file; only the homegrown build guard is duplicated rather than centralized.

evidence: app/vite.config.js:5 — output: 'server' is the only documented Gracile mode that satisfies the spec's requirement to fetch all data over HTTP at request time (no build-time prerender), used consistently (app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].js:155)

app/src/routes/(home).client.js:40-50 — fetch+DOMParser+history delivers the required debounced search and URL-synced filters without touching the experimental CSR add-on: same behavior, none of the risk
app/package.json:11 — exact pin (no caret) of the 0.x framework is the correct hedge for pre-1.0 churn; carets reserved for the 1.0+ deps (lit, express, vite)
app/package.json:14 — gratuitous: Vite 8 buys nothing the app needs; Gracile's peer range equally allows Vite 7
app/vite.config.js:5 — gratuitous: trailingSlash: 'ignore' restates the documented default

app/src/document.js:14 — the new URL(…, import.meta.url) convenience buys one line of brevity at the cost of relying on a pattern Vite documents as unsupported in SSR (and which demonstrably orphans the stylesheet in the production build)
justification.rationale: The choices that matter are principled — server output is the only spec-compliant strategy, vanilla-JS progressive enhancement avoids every experimental surface, and the 0.x pin hedges churn — but Vite 8 adds nothing, one option restates a default, and one Vite pattern steps outside documented support.

findings.issue: Stylesheet href built with new URL('./document.css', import.meta.url).pathname, a pattern Vite's current docs say 'Does not work with SSR'. The production server bundle leaves it untransformed (app/dist/server/chunk/document.js:12), so the runtime href is a dead filesystem path (…/dist/server/chunk/document.css) that express.static never serves, while the real stylesheet is emitted orphaned at app/dist/client/assets/document-CKJfxvWA.css — production pages ship without the global stylesheet or design tokens.
findings.suggestion: Use the pattern Gracile's document docs prescribe — reference the stylesheet by its project-root path (e.g. <link rel="stylesheet" href="/src/document.css" />), which Gracile's document pipeline resolves in dev and rewrites for the production client build.

findings.issue: GRACILE_BUILD=1 is a homegrown environment variable whose GRACILE_ prefix mimics a framework contract; no such variable exists in @gracile/engine or the Gracile docs. It is guarded by a copy-pasted BUILDING() helper in six route handlers (e.g. app/src/routes/(home).js:15, app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].js:23), and in server output mode route handlers are not executed at build time, so the guard appears to protect nothing.
findings.suggestion: Verify whether any build-time handler execution actually occurs; if not, remove the flag entirely. If kept, centralize the check in src/lib/ under an app-owned name (e.g. POKDEX_SKIP_FETCH) so it cannot be mistaken for a framework API.

findings.issue: Vite 8 (major line stable only since March 2026) is chosen although nothing in the app requires it and Gracile's peer range (^7.0.0 || ^8.0.0) equally supports Vite 7, stacking an extra layer of very-recent software under an already 0.x framework.
findings.suggestion: Pin the older supported major unless a Vite 8 feature is needed, or document the deliberate choice to track the newest supported line and budget for it at minor bumps.

findings.issue: trailingSlash: 'ignore' restates the documented default value of the option (user-config: "@defaultValue 'ignore'"), suggesting copy-paste rather than intent.
findings.suggestion: Drop the redundant option, or keep it with a comment explaining why the default is being pinned explicitly.

findings.issue: The entire application rests on pre-1.0 @gracile/gracile 0.11.0 (published ~6 months ago); under 0.x semver, breaking changes can arrive in any minor release, so every documented-stable API used here is still churn-prone. This risk is inherent to the assigned framework and well mitigated by the exact pin.
findings.suggestion: Keep the exact version pin and schedule a review of every 0.x minor upgrade (the framework's own CONTRIBUTING notes it is sub-1.x); avoid loosening to a caret range.

summary: The app reaches for essentially nothing experimental: no framework flags, no @gracile-labs add-ons, no experimental CSR or hydration — interactivity is hand-rolled with stable web APIs, every framework import matches the current documented stable surface, and the 0.x framework is exact-pinned. Its newness is structural and largely unavoidable: a pre-1.0 framework ~6 months old and Vite 8 underpin everything, well contained behind a single document/api/components trio and a 6-line config. The one genuine break from documented-stable behavior is the new URL(…, import.meta.url) stylesheet reference, which Vite documents as not working in SSR and which the shipped build confirms orphans the CSS in production.
